walkthrough:
Evaluate the derivative at $x = 1$ to find the tangent gradient:
$$f'(1) = 8(2(1) - 3)^{1/3} - 10(1)^{2/3} = 8(-1)^{1/3} - 10(1) = 8(-1) - 10 = -18$$

Form the equation of the normal line passing through $(1, 0)$:
$$y - 0 = \frac{1}{18}(x - 1) \implies y = \frac{x - 1}{18}$$

Calculate the discriminant of the equation $125x^2 - 128x + 192 = 0$ corresponding to $f'(x) = 0$:
$$\Delta = b^2 - 4ac = (-128)^2 - 4(125)(192) = 16384 - 96000 = -79616 < 0$$

Deduce that there are no stationary points on the curve:
$$\text{Since } \Delta < 0, \text{ the equation } f'(x) = 0 \text{ has no real solutions, so } f'(x) \text{ never crosses zero for } x > 0.$$

Evaluate the sign of $f'(x)$ at a sample domain point (e.g. $x = 1$):
$$f'(1) = -18 < 0 \implies f'(x) < 0 \text{ for all } x > 0$$
$$\text{Therefore, } f \text{ is a strictly decreasing function.}$$
